doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Cleveland and his mother the seamstress
summary: He grew up in cold Cleveland; his mother was a seamstress who loved her Singer machine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Tell us a little bit on the personal side – first of all, we haven’t established that you grew up in Cleveland. So you want to – it’s Cleveland, Ohio.
Ohio. Coldest place I’ve ever been.
Cold. It’s cold in Cleveland. What did your dad do for a living? And what did your mom do for a living?
Mom, if she’d have been supported by my father, she could have been – she was a seamstress.
Right. Like my mom. She could sew.
And could design dresses and make a . . .
When Singer sewing machines came out, that was her dream.
To own a Singer sewing machine.
To have that Singer sewing – she finally got it, and everybody in the neighborhood – all the women . . .
Came over to Mom and had her make her . . .
Oh yeah. [?] had her do the seam or fix [?]. She’d get on the sewing machine and show them how to put those seams in, and different things that she learned with the machine.
